changes.text: Unreal SDK installation now rejects incomplete native headers before changing the game project.
Hub and Studio downloads support the new release archive layout on GitHub and COS.
Hub and Studio update checks and downloads use the active release sources after the Harken rename.
Command-line update checks can verify Hub or Studio independently.
Unity and Unreal projects share one SDK workflow with separate project association, SDK actions, and results.
Project association now explains that it only adds or removes the project pair from the integration list.
Check the installed SDK without selecting a source. Failures explain their causes, recovery steps, and available actions.
SDK changes use dedicated dialogs and safety checks that require closing the target game project before writing files.
SDK scans run in the background with live activity and a Stop Scan button. Stopped scans cannot approve SDK changes.
Choose an Unreal SDK folder under Plugins, migrate with a verified backup, and recover interrupted migrations through the shared SDK workflow.
Hub manages SDK integration independently, including repair guidance for damaged installations in Chinese and English.
Choose a custom SDK installation folder inside your Unity project. Hub remembers the location for each project.
Move an installed SDK without reinstalling it or unlinking projects, preserving modified files and Unity asset references.
SDK migration creates a verified backup and supports restoring the original location after an interruption.
SDK operations detect duplicate installations and reject unsafe paths, conflicting package references, or projects open in Unity.
Integration guidance now explains how to unlink projects or migrate the SDK, with consistent Chinese and English text.
On Windows, Hub restores its window after an update and confirms startup before reporting a successful restart.
Reinstalling a Hub update on Windows no longer replaces its running update helper or leaves later updates blocked by files in use.
The Unreal project selection button is temporarily hidden in Engine Integrations.
The integration editor opens without waiting for Studio version checks to finish.
Reduced delays when browsing for or selecting a Harken project.
Integration checks, installation, and removal now show their own results, with failures selected first and empty details hidden.
Removed release notes for Hub versions older than 0.1.47 from the About window.
Remove multiple selected projects from the list at once, without deleting their files.
Manual Studio package installation now explains folder conflicts and rejects packages for a different operating system.
Language names stay in their native language when switching the Hub interface language.
Template selection is temporarily hidden when creating a project.
Updated the Harken Studio license agreement and privacy policy. Hub asks you to confirm the revised terms.
The Hub website link now opens https://harken.xd.com.
Hub stays usable while Studio creates a project, without closing Studio when creation takes longer than expected.
Pending update files survive cache cleanup, and missing files or failed downloads can recover without waiting for a new release.
Hub stays open and explains the error if its update helper cannot be started.
Unreal plugin updates preserve hidden project-specific files and files inside hidden folders.
Read the license agreement and privacy policy side by side from the Settings menu.
Install and keep older Studio versions, and open their existing projects with the selected version.
Installation issues now show specific causes and let you select which installation to repair. Missing newer Hub features no longer mark an intact older version as damaged.
Hub recommends the Studio version last used to save each project. Your chosen installation takes priority; if several installations match, Hub asks you to choose.
Before upgrading a project, Hub shows the affected files and asks for confirmation. Cancelling leaves the project unchanged.
If Hub cannot finish checking a project, Studio can continue the checks and ask you to confirm any upgrade before opening it.
Studio stays open while you decide whether to upgrade a project, even if its connection to Hub is lost.
The project list now loads project details in the background.
Hub automatically checks local Studio builds again after recompilation. Unavailable installations remain listed separately.
Studio packages in the old format can no longer be installed or used with this Hub version. Use a package in the new format.
